inspector.observationHint: Wavelengths sampled by the elements that depend on the band (stars, scenes, lamps).
inspector.selectionHint: Shift+click adds to the selection; Shift+drag, or a drag in the selection mode (V), selects a zone.
inspector.randomnessHint: Seed of every random process of the context (noise, turbulence, Monte-Carlo draws): the same seed gives the same results.

python.title: Equivalent Python script

discard.title: Unsaved changes

shortcuts.pan: Move the view, whatever the pointer mode

quickAdd.placeholder: Element to add… (e.g. thin lens, camera)

run.archive: Archive the results of the runs

results.empty: Run the context (Ctrl+Enter), or click an output of a block to inspect it.

journal.empty: Nothing yet: runs and actions appear here as they happen.

presets.title: Presets
presets.welcomeHint: Simulate light from a source to a detector with blocks. Start from a preset, or take the guided tour.
presets.orBuild: …or build your own: drag elements from the palette on the left.

welcome.title: Welcome to LUMOS
welcome.text: LUMOS simulates how light travels through an instrument: from a source, through optical elements, to a detector. We have opened a first simulation for you.

palette.title: The elements
palette.text: Every element of the library is here, by category: sources, telescopes, optics, detectors, processing… Drag one onto the canvas, or click it.

canvas.title: The optical system
canvas.text: Blocks are connected by wires: light flows from left to right. Drag from an output (right of a block) to an input (left) to connect; the colour of a port tells the kind of light it carries.

block.title: A block
block.text: Each block shows its name, its type and a few values. Click it to select it.

inspector.title: Its parameters
inspector.text: The inspector shows the parameters of the selected block, with their units: type a value (e.g. 3 mm) and press Enter. Ctrl+Z undoes any change.

run.title: Run the simulation
run.text: Run computes the outputs of the context. Press Next: we run it for you (Ctrl+Enter does it too).

results.title: The results
results.text: Each output appears with its figure and its statistics, with units. Download the figure, the data or the whole signal.

inspect.title: Look anywhere
inspect.text: Click the name of any output of a block to see the light at that point, without running everything.

files.title: Keep your work
files.text: Save the context as a .lumos file, open one, or get the equivalent Python script.

help.title: Help
help.text: Replay this tour at any time, and press ? for the keyboard shortcuts.

done.title: Your turn!
done.text: Change a value and run again, or open another preset. The documentation explains the physics of every element.

operation.disabled: The operation of equipment is disabled on this instance: actions only change the simulation (digital twin).
operation.operatorOnly: Only operators drive equipment: log in as an operator.
operation.addresses: Addresses of the devices (one per line)
operation.noAction: No element of this context has actions.
operation.stopHint: Emergency stop of every device of the context
operation.confirmText: {{action}} will drive the device {{device}}. Check that the bench is safe.

account.signHint: Sign this challenge with your SSH key (valid 2 minutes, once):
account.loginHint: Paste the signature printed by ssh-keygen below.

assistant.keyHint: The assistant is Claude, called from your browser with your own key (console.anthropic.com). The key stays in this tab and goes to the Claude API only, never to the LUMOS server; requests are billed to your account.
assistant.empty: Ask in plain language: "add a camera after the lens", "why is the image under-sampled?", "run it and give me the contrast between 3 and 4 λ/D".
assistant.truncated: The answer was cut: ask for a shorter one.
assistant.tooLong: Stopped after 25 steps: ask again to continue.
assistant.badKey: The API key was refused: check it, or forget it and give another one.
assistant.confirmTitle: The assistant asks for a confirmation
assistant.settingsHint: The assistant is a language model of your choice, called from your browser with your own account. Your key stays in this tab and goes to its provider only, never to the LUMOS server; requests are billed to your account.
assistant.keyKept: kept in this tab: leave empty to keep it
assistant.keyMissing: Give an API key, or log in.
assistant.modelMissing: Give the name of a model.
assistant.urlMissing: Give the address of the endpoint (…/v1).
assistant.popupBlocked: The login window was blocked: allow popups for this site.
assistant.figureShown: a figure is shown to the user

about.anthropic: Claude with an API key of the Anthropic console. A Claude.ai subscription cannot be used by other applications: to use it, add LUMOS to Claude as an MCP connector instead (see the documentation).
about.openai: OpenAI models with an API key of the OpenAI platform (a ChatGPT subscription does not give API access).
about.gemini: Gemini with a key of Google AI Studio (free tier available), through its OpenAI-compatible endpoint.
about.openrouter: Log in with your OpenRouter account (no key to copy: OpenRouter creates one for LUMOS, with your credits and limits), or paste a key. OpenRouter gives access to the models of most providers, Claude, GPT and Gemini included.
about.custom: Any endpoint of the OpenAI chat completions API with tools: Mistral, Groq, DeepSeek, or a model on your machine with Ollama (http://localhost:11434/v1), LM Studio or vLLM. The endpoint must accept requests from this page (CORS).

prior.free: Free this parameter: give it a prior for Monte-Carlo runs
prior.edit: Edit the prior of this free parameter
prior.hint: Monte-Carlo runs draw this parameter from its prior.

study.title: Study
study.sweepHint: Run the context for a range of values of some parameters.
study.sampleHint: Draw the free parameters from their priors, and the noise, many times.
study.unitsHint: Values in the unit of the parameter, or with their own unit ("190 mm").
study.noFree: No free parameter and no noise: free a parameter with the dice button of the inspector.
study.noFreeNoise: No free parameter: every draw repeats the run with its own noise.
study.noOutputs: The context has no output to compute.
study.independentHint: Each point draws its own noise realization (seed {{seed}}); otherwise every point has the same noise.
study.empty: No study yet: sweep parameters or run a Monte-Carlo study of the context.
study.loopHint: Run the feedback loops of the context step by step.
study.noFeedback: No feedback yet: select the block computing the correction and close the loop in its inspector.
study.loopDetails: Each step computes the outputs, applies the feedbacks, then advances the clock by the period. The loop keeps its final state (Undo puts it back).

feedback.hint: An output of this block drives a field at the next step of a loop (Study, Loop): "+=" adds the value, "=" sets it.
feedback.title: {{source}} drives {{target}} at the next step ({{mode}})
